subject: Efficient staff storage
hook: Turning a cluttered staff room into fitted storage takes six steps. Here they are.
ig:
Turning a cluttered staff room into fitted storage takes six steps. Here they are.

Commercial storage projects follow the same path as a home project, with one extra thing to plan around: the business still has to run.

1. Walk-round with the person who manages the space.
2. A storage list, sized to the actual team, not a guess.
3. A layout that uses full wall height and any alcoves.
4. Furniture made and assembled in our Hanley workshop.
5. An installation plan agreed with you to keep the working day as undisturbed as possible.
6. Handover, with every item given a home.

The most valuable step is usually number 2. Counting coats, lockers and boxes stops you building too little, which is how staff rooms end up cluttered again within months.

Save this if you're planning an office refresh, and share it with whoever signs off the budget.
fb:
Thinking about sorting out the staff room or office storage? Here's what the process looks like with us.

It starts with a walk-round and a proper count of what needs storing, so the furniture is sized for your team rather than guessed. Then it's designed, made and assembled in our Hanley workshop, and our own team fits it at a time agreed with you.

We've laid out the typical stages in this carousel. If you'd like to see finished work from our workshop, it's all here:

on_asset: F1: Walk-round — We look at the space with whoever manages it and note what's being stored where, and what's ending up on the floor. | F2: Storage list — Coats, lockers, kitchen supplies, stationery and files are counted, so the design is sized to the team. | F3: Layout and finishes — A plan that uses full wall heights and alcoves, in finishes that suit the rest of the building. | F4: Workshop build — Cut, edged, drilled and assembled in Hanley, then checked before it leaves. | F5: Fit plan — The install is scheduled with you to keep disruption to the working day as low as possible. | F6: Everything has a home — Clear worktops, coats off chairs, supplies in one place. | Label: Concept image (representative process)
